lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hello Keisha, it's Ana. Do you have a few minutes for our call?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hey, yeah, I was waiting for your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Here's what I had in mind for today, but tell me if you'd rather focus on something else.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Any problems this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good. Busy, but good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's great to hear.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Tell me how the walking went this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Honestly, not much. With my feet like this I don't trust myself.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: When I walk I sleep better, I noticed that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know where the day goes. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: The days got away from you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walking fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've always eaten late, that's how we do it at home.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So it's not that you don't care. It's that the numbness in your feet keeps getting in the way.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe after the summer.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the walking going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hmm, I have to think about that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Work has been crazy, I'm doing overtime. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're giving everything to work right now, and there's not much left over for you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I like what I eat. I'm not going to change at my age.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, the numbness in your feet makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've tried this before and it never lasts.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So it's not that you don't care. It's that the numbness in your feet keeps getting in the way.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: There's no sidewalk on my street and cars go really fast.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd walk more if you had a place that felt safe.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people walk inside the mall early, before the stores open. It's cool and it's flat.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Let's say I walk 15 minutes on 3 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I'll ask my son to come with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 0 out of 4 days, the hard part was the numbness in your feet, and next week you're going to walk 15 minutes on 3 days. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Keisha, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

tags.note: Agenda offered with invitation to change focus
Barrier: numbness, doubts about walking safely
Adds meaning beyond the barrier stated
Eating habits as reason to stay same
Reflects openness plus need for fit
Past failures as reason not to try
Verbatim repeat of line 19; ignores 'never lasts'
Mall walking option offered after permission

flags.reason: Verbatim repeat of line 19 in response to 'never lasts'; misses the participant's expressed hopelessness about sustaining change.
Verbatim repeat of line 24 rather than a fresh reflection of the participant's last statement.
Numbness in feet with 'I don't trust myself' and unsafe street was not explored for fall risk or clinician input.
Participant asked to move the call later; coach did not acknowledge or confirm the new time.

score.summary: Keisha shared real barriers (foot numbness, unsafe street, work overtime) and the coach used autonomy-supporting reflections well, leading to a concrete goal of 15 minutes on three days. Coaching slipped in places: two reflections were repeated verbatim, the fall-risk implication of the numbness was not explored, and her request to reschedule was not addressed.
strengths: Line 23 and 28: emphasizes Keisha's autonomy and expertise on her schedule.
Line 31: clear double-sided reflection that names her ambivalence.
Line 46: asks permission (line 44) before offering the mall-walking idea.
Line 54: clear summary before closing, with a concrete goal set at line 50.
coaching_tips: Line 35 repeats line 19 word for word; respond to 'I've tried this before and it never lasts' (line 34) with a fresh reflection of the hopelessness and past effort.
Line 9: ask about the numbness and balance before building a walking plan, e.g., whether she has checked with her care team about walking safely.
Line 57: acknowledge the request to move the call later and confirm the new time before closing.
Line 56: the text-midweek and two-week call plan should be confirmed with the new time she asked for.
